scenes.visual: Title card 'Two Animals on One Plot' fades in over a cartoon mussel and a cartoon crab on a sandy shore. Same world and colour map as the first film. THE WORLD, kept for both films (16:9, warm cream background, flat cartoon shapes, no molecular structures). COLOUR MAP, same in every scene and in the second film: INSIDE (the regulated variable) = TEAL bar or level, labelled with the variable's name; OUTSIDE = ORANGE bar or level; LEAK = ORANGE arrow from outside toward inside, its thickness = the actual leak flow, which grows with the gap between outside and inside; PUSH-BACK = TEAL arrow pointing toward the set point, its thickness = the actual push-back flow, which grows with the gap from the set point; whenever the inside has settled, the two arrows are drawn equally thick, at every dial setting. STRENGTHS are dials, never arrows: LEAK STRENGTH = ORANGE dial, PUSH-BACK STRENGTH = TEAL dial; the fraction leak strength ÷ (leak strength + push-back strength) compares the dials. SET POINT = dashed TEAL line. Loop parts always named in this order and these words: regulated variable, set point, sensor, integrator, effector. Anything not computed is labelled 'schematic'.

scenes.tts: Move a mussel and a shore crab from seawater into water diluted to half strength. Whose blood follows the water? The first film built a dial: push-back strength against leak strength. Now we read that dial off real animals.
scenes.visual: A tank of seawater, tinted ORANGE, holds a mussel and a crab. A jug pours fresh water in; the ORANGE tint pales and a label reads 'half-strength seawater'. A question mark hovers between the two animals. A small inset of the first film's two dials, ORANGE 'leak strength' and TEAL 'push-back strength', slides in at the corner.
scenes.narration: Move a mussel and a shore crab from seawater into water diluted to half strength. Whose blood follows the water? The first film built a dial: push-back strength against leak strength. Now we read that dial off real animals.

scenes.tts: Draw a plot. Across the bottom goes the water's osmolality, the concentration of dissolved particles. Up the side goes the blood's osmolality. Orange marks the outside, teal the inside, as before.
scenes.visual: Empty axes draw on. x axis in ORANGE: 'water osmolality (outside)', low on the left (dilute) to high on the right (full seawater). y axis in TEAL: 'blood osmolality (inside)'. Label 'schematic'.
scenes.narration: Draw a plot. Across the bottom goes the water's osmolality, the concentration of dissolved particles. Up the side goes the blood's osmolality. Orange marks the outside, teal the inside, as before.

scenes.tts: Draw the diagonal first. Along it, blood equals water. That is a perfect conformer. Then draw a flat line. Along it, the blood stays put as the water changes. That is a perfect regulator, over the range it survives.
scenes.visual: A grey diagonal draws from bottom left to top right, labelled 'blood = water: ideal conformer'. Then a flat TEAL line draws across at a fixed height, spanning only the middle of the x axis, labelled 'blood held: ideal regulator (over the range it survives)'.
scenes.narration: Draw the diagonal first. Along it, blood equals water. That is a perfect conformer. Then draw a flat line. Along it, the blood stays put as the water changes. That is a perfect regulator, over the range it survives.

scenes.tts: The slope of an animal's line is the share of the outside change that gets inside. In the simple model, steep means leak is much stronger. Flat means push-back is much stronger. A line halfway between means the two are about equally strong.
scenes.visual: The first film's ORANGE leak-strength dial and TEAL push-back-strength dial appear beside the plot. A step triangle on the diagonal shows 'outside change' along x and 'inside change' up y; caption 'slope = leak strength ÷ (leak strength + push-back strength), in the simple model'. As the TEAL dial turns up, a test line rotates from the diagonal toward flat.
scenes.narration: The slope of an animal's line is the share of the outside change that gets inside. In the simple model, steep means leak is much stronger. Flat means push-back is much stronger. A line halfway between means the two are about equally strong.

scenes.tts: Now the blue mussel, Mytilus edulis. Dilute its water, and over the salinities it tolerates, its blood comes close to the water around it. Its points fall along the diagonal. For blood osmolality, the mussel conforms. That label covers this one variable.
scenes.visual: A cartoon blue mussel slides in. Dots labelled 'mussel' drop onto the plot one at a time as the water value moves left, each landing on or near the grey diagonal. Label 'conformer' glows by the mussel. Label 'schematic'.
scenes.narration: Now the blue mussel, Mytilus edulis. Dilute its water, and over the salinities it tolerates, its blood comes close to the water around it. Its points fall along the diagonal. For blood osmolality, the mussel conforms. That label covers this one variable.

scenes.tts: Now the shore crab, Carcinus maenas. In full-strength seawater, its blood sits close to the water, near the diagonal. So far, the crab looks just like the mussel.
scenes.visual: A cartoon green shore crab scuttles in. At the right end of the plot (full seawater), a dot labelled 'crab' lands on the diagonal.
scenes.narration: Now the shore crab, Carcinus maenas. In full-strength seawater, its blood sits close to the water, near the diagonal. So far, the crab looks just like the mussel.

scenes.tts: Now dilute the water to half strength. Will the crab's blood sit on the diagonal, on the flat line, or in between?
scenes.visual: A marker slides left along the x axis to 'half strength'. A ghost dot hovers with three dashed options: on the diagonal, on the flat line, between. Option cards: 'diagonal', 'flat', 'between'.
scenes.narration: Now dilute the water to half strength. Will the crab's blood sit on the diagonal, on the flat line, or in between?

scenes.visual: Hold. The ghost dot blinks among the three positions. Countdown ring fills.

scenes.tts: In between. The crab holds its blood well above the water. Its line bends flatter in dilute water. So the crab conforms at one end of its range and regulates at the other.
scenes.visual: The 'between' card lights. Crab dots fill in: along the diagonal at the right, then bending flatter toward the left, staying well above the diagonal. A TEAL push-back arrow appears at the bent part, pointing up toward the crab's line (an actual pull, not drawn to a measured size). Labels: 'conforms here' at right, 'regulates here' at left. Label 'schematic'.
scenes.narration: In between. The crab holds its blood well above the water. Its line bends flatter in dilute water. So the crab conforms at one end of its range and regulates at the other.

scenes.tts: So regulator and conformer describe one variable over one range. They never describe a whole animal. Name one variable and a stated range before you choose a label.
scenes.visual: Two brackets under the crab's line: the right bracket 'conformer (this range)', the left 'regulator (this range)'. A stamp 'one variable, one range' presses onto the plot.
scenes.narration: So regulator and conformer describe one variable over one range. They never describe a whole animal. Name one variable and a stated range before you choose a label.

scenes.tts: Now a second plot, for temperature. Outside temperature goes across. Body temperature goes up. Over the air temperatures a person can bear, an adult human regulates core temperature. That gives a nearly flat line.
scenes.visual: The osmolality plot slides to the left half of the screen and stays, titled 'blood salt'. A second, separate set of axes draws on the right half, titled 'temperature': x in ORANGE 'outside temperature', y in TEAL 'body (core) temperature'. A cartoon adult human appears; a nearly flat TEAL line draws across a bracketed middle stretch of the x axis labelled 'tolerable range', labelled 'adult human: regulates core temperature'. Label 'schematic'.
scenes.narration: Now a second plot, for temperature. Outside temperature goes across. Body temperature goes up. Over the air temperatures a person can bear, an adult human regulates core temperature. That gives a nearly flat line.

scenes.tts: A typical fish in a lake gives a line near the diagonal. Its body temperature largely follows the water.
scenes.visual: On the right-hand temperature plot only, a cartoon lake fish swims in; its line draws close to the grey diagonal, labelled 'lake fish: largely follows the water'. Label 'schematic'.
scenes.narration: A typical fish in a lake gives a line near the diagonal. Its body temperature largely follows the water.

scenes.tts: Two plots, one dial. Each line's slope is the share of an outside change that gets inside. It holds for that variable, over that range. In the simple model, that slope reads the dial.
scenes.visual: Both plots side by side, never merged. Left, 'blood salt': mussel line near the diagonal and crab line bending, each tagged with its name and icon. Right, 'temperature': human line flat over the tolerable range, fish line near the diagonal, each tagged with its name and icon. A small pair of ORANGE leak-strength and TEAL push-back-strength dials sits by each line, set to match its slope. Label 'schematic'.
scenes.narration: Two plots, one dial. Each line's slope is the share of an outside change that gets inside. It holds for that variable, over that range. In the simple model, that slope reads the dial.

scenes.visual: End card with Hex, the hexagon mascot, beside the line: 'Regulator or conformer: one variable, one range, never a whole animal.' Same ORANGE and TEAL colours.
